name: skills
description: The open agent skills tool - npx skills
readmeExcerpt:
# skills The CLI for the open agent skills ecosystem. Agent skills are reusable instructions that teach coding agents how to perform tasks, from reviewing code to working with a library. Discover skills at [skills.sh](https://skills.sh). Supports **OpenCode**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, and [75 more](docs/agents.md).

## Install a Skill Requires Node.js 22.20 or later. Run this from your project: ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills ``` Choose the skills and coding agents to install to. Skills are installed to the current project by default; add `-g` to make them available across projects. ```bash # Choose one skill and agent npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines -a claude-code # Browse available skills npx skills find ``` See the [installation reference](docs/commands.md#skills-add) for source formats, private repositories, and all options. ## Other Commands | Command | Description | | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | | `npx skills find [query]` | Search for skills | | `npx skills list` | List installed skills | | `npx skills use @` | Use one skill without installing | | `npx skills check` | Check for available updates | | `npx skills update [skills...]` | Update installed skills | | `npx skills remove [skills...]` | Remove installed skills | | `npx skills init [name]` | Create a skill template | Read the [CLI reference](docs/commands.md) or run `npx skills --help` for examples and options. Experimental commands are listed [below](#experimental-features). ## Use a Skill Without Installing Generate a prompt for a skill, or launch a supported coding agent with it: ```bash npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines --agent claude-code ``` Omit `--agent` to print the prompt instead. See [`skills use`](docs/commands.md#skills-use). ## Experimental Features
Commands prefixed with experimental_ are previews. Their names, options, and behavior may change or be removed in any release without notice. | Command | Description | | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | | `npx skills experimental_sync` | Sync skills shipped by npm dependencies into your project | | `npx skills experimental_install` | Restore project skills recorded in `skills-lock.json` | Some npm packages bundle instructions for your agent alongside their code. Sync links them into your project so they update with the dependency, and also installs skill packs declared in `package.json`: ```bash npm install -D skills agent-browser npx skills experimental_sync -y ``` See the [experimental commands reference](docs/commands.md#experimental-commands) for options, the `skills` field, and the [RFC](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/2323) behind it.
## Supported Agents The CLI detects installed agents and lets you choose where skills are installed. See [all supported agents, installation paths, and compatibility](docs/agents.md). ## Creating Skills ```bash npx skills init my-skill ``` Edit the generated `SKILL.md` with instructions for your agent. See [creating and sharing skills](docs/creating-skills.md) for the format and discovery rules. ## Documentation - [CLI reference](docs/commands.md): installation, command examples, and experimental features - [Supported agents](docs/agents.md): agent names, skill directories, and compatibility - [Creating skills](docs/creating-skills.md): frontmatter, repository layouts, and plugins - [Troubleshooting and configuration](docs/troubleshooting.md): common problems, environment variables, and telemetry - [Programmatic API](docs/api.md): install and manage skills from your own tools with `import { installSkills } from 'skills'` ## Telemetry The CLI collects anonymous usage data. Set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` to disable telemetry and security-audit requests. See [what is collected](docs/troubleshooting.md#telemetry). ## Related Links - [Skills Directory](https://skills.sh) - [Agent Skills Specification](https://agentskills.io) - [Vercel Agent Skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) ## License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
readmeHtml:
skills

The CLI for the open agent skills ecosystem.

Agent skills are reusable instructions that teach coding agents how to perform tasks, from reviewing code to working with a library. Discover skills at skills.sh.

Supports OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and 75 more.

Install a Skill

Requires Node.js 22.20 or later. Run this from your project:

npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills

Choose the skills and coding agents to install to. Skills are installed to the current project by default; add -g to make them available across projects.

# Choose one skill and agent
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines -a claude-code

# Browse available skills
npx skills find

See the installation reference for source formats, private repositories, and all options.

Other Commands

Command Description
npx skills find [query] Search for skills
npx skills list List installed skills
npx skills use <source>@<skill> Use one skill without installing
npx skills check Check for available updates
npx skills update [skills...] Update installed skills
npx skills remove [skills...] Remove installed skills
npx skills init [name] Create a skill template

Read the CLI reference or run npx skills --help for examples and options. Experimental commands are listed below.

Use a Skill Without Installing

Generate a prompt for a skill, or launch a supported coding agent with it:

npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines --agent claude-code

Omit --agent to print the prompt instead. See skills use.

Experimental Features

Commands prefixed with experimental_ are previews. Their names, options, and behavior may change or be removed in any release without notice.
Command Description
npx skills experimental_sync Sync skills shipped by npm dependencies into your project
npx skills experimental_install Restore project skills recorded in skills-lock.json

Some npm packages bundle instructions for your agent alongside their code. Sync links them into your project so they update with the dependency, and also installs skill packs declared in package.json:

npm install -D skills agent-browser
npx skills experimental_sync -y

See the experimental commands reference for options, the skills field, and the RFC behind it.

Supported Agents

The CLI detects installed agents and lets you choose where skills are installed. See all supported agents, installation paths, and compatibility.

Creating Skills

npx skills init my-skill

Edit the generated SKILL.md with instructions for your agent. See creating and sharing skills for the format and discovery rules.

Documentation

  • CLI reference: installation, command examples, and experimental features
  • Supported agents: agent names, skill directories, and compatibility
  • Creating skills: frontmatter, repository layouts, and plugins
  • Troubleshooting and configuration: common problems, environment variables, and telemetry
  • Programmatic API: install and manage skills from your own tools with import { installSkills } from 'skills'

Telemetry

The CLI collects anonymous usage data. Set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 to disable telemetry and security-audit requests. See what is collected.

Related Links

  • Skills Directory
  • Agent Skills Specification
  • Vercel Agent Skills

License

This project is licensed under the MIT License.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A unified command-line interface for managing and distributing specialized skills across various AI coding agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project provides a unified command-line interface for the open agent skills ecosystem, acting as a specialized package manager. It allows developers to easily install and utilize specialized capabilities across a wide array of popular AI coding agents, including OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. The tool resolves sources from public GitHub repositories, private GitLab instances, or local file paths, and directly injects them into the agent's context. By establishing a standardized way to share, configure, and consume agent skills, it significantly enhances the practical utility and consistency of AI coding assistants across different development environments.
keyFeatures: Broad agent compatibility: Supports over 70 different AI coding agents natively, including popular choices like Claude Code and Cursor.
Flexible source resolution: Installs skills directly from GitHub shorthands, full URLs, specific directory paths, or local folders.
Private repository support: Seamlessly utilizes existing local Git authentication to fetch private skills hosted in enterprise repositories.
Interactive agent launching: Generates a prompt for a specific skill and immediately launches a supported interactive coding agent session.
Standardized skill sharing: Provides a common ecosystem and distribution mechanism for teams to share custom agent capabilities.

useCases.title: Agent capability extension
useCases.description: A developer installs a specialized web design guidelines skill to ensure their AI coding assistant adheres to specific CSS standards.

useCases.title: Cross-agent skill sharing
useCases.description: An engineering team writes a custom deployment skill and shares it across different agents used by various team members.

useCases.title: Private tool distribution
useCases.description: A company distributes proprietary internal development tools as reusable agent skills via a private GitLab repository.

useCases.title: Interactive prompt generation
useCases.description: A user leverages the CLI to quickly generate a complex prompt from a skill template before feeding it into their preferred LLM.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Next.js developers and AI practitioners looking for practical examples of integrating various AI models and services into web applications. The repository offers comprehensive, production-ready examples.
